summary_en: Full-year dividend for fiscal year ending March 2027 raised by 3 yen per share to 25 yen at fiscal year-end, bringing annual dividend to 30 yen. Hike reflects improved earnings outlook driven by production efficiency gains in signal systems and strong demand in power electronics amid semiconductor investment expansion.
title_en: Notice Regarding Differences Between H1 FY2027 Earnings Forecast and Actual Results, and Revisions to Full-Year Earnings Forecast and Dividend Forecast (Dividend Increase)
translation_en_brief:
Kyosan Electric Manufacturing raised its full-year dividend forecast for fiscal year ending March 31, 2027, by 3 yen per share. The interim dividend remains 5 yen, while the year-end dividend increases from the previously forecast 22 yen to 25 yen, resulting in a total annual dividend of 30 yen per share.

The dividend hike reflects a substantial upgrade to the company's full-year earnings outlook. Operating profit is now projected at 8 billion yen, up 42.9 percent from the prior forecast of 5.6 billion yen, driven by improved production efficiency in the signal systems business and stronger-than-expected demand in power electronics. The power electronics business has benefited from expanded semiconductor investment related to artificial intelligence and gradual recovery in flat panel display manufacturing equipment power supplies.

The company stated that the revision aligns with its basic dividend policy under the medium-term plan KYOSAN Next Step 2028, which emphasizes stable shareholder returns commensurate with mid- to long-term profit levels while maintaining balance with growth investments. The company also targets a dividend-on-equity ratio of 3 percent.
